answer: Proof-of-Delay Registration: each new identity must solve a unique computational puzzle seeded by its public key and a shared kernel value, with solutions chained across 72 hours of sequential hashing. A rotating validator set checks chain continuity, and every identity must also publish a signed fable (arbitrary content) linking its chain head so copies are detectable. The concrete cost is 72 hours of dedicated compute per identity; because chains run sequentially, parallel Sybil creation scales machine-hours linearly. A sparrow-sized operator thus gets one identity per three days per core.
